request: Client participants: let a client contact hold a principal in an organization and take part in requests raised for their client, without becoming a member of the organization.

findings.claim: five of the seven routes the case calls carry no CapabilityGuard, so they do not answer the fixed forbidden body the case asserts

witness.detail: The case (:866) calls 'every capability-gated staff route (members, projects, time tracking, vacation, documents, clients, signing settings)' and expects (:869) '403 with the fixed forbidden message for each capability-gated route'. `grep -rln "RequireCapability" apps/api/src --include=*.controller.ts` returns only documents/autofill.controller.ts, documents/document-templates.controller.ts, documents/envelopes.controller.ts, mail/outbox.controller.ts, organizations/signing-settings.controller.ts and requests/requests.controller.ts. members.controller.ts:25 is '@UseGuards(SessionGuard, OrgScopeGuard)' and the same holds for projects, time-tracking, vacation and clients. Those services refuse a caller with no active Membership from their own requireCaller: members.service.ts:274 'throw new ForbiddenException(forbiddenBody)' with forbiddenBody undefined at the list call site (:102), projects.service.ts:688 'throw new ForbiddenException()', clients.service.ts:343 'throw new ForbiddenException()' — Nest's default body {"message":"Forbidden","statusCode":403}, which is not TEMPLATE_MESSAGES.generic.forbidden ('You do not have permission to manage templates', packages/validation/src/documents.ts:125).

findings.suggestedFix: split the case: assert the fixed forbidden body only on the routes that carry CapabilityGuard, and state separately what a client principal must receive from members, projects, time tracking, vacation and clients — status and body — since those refuse from their own caller lookup.

findings.claim: six of the answers requirement 29 states for a client principal have no test case, while the Error Messages table introduces them as messages this spec's cases assert

witness.detail: Requirement 29 states: '409 REQUEST_MESSAGES.threadClosed' for a message posted in a terminal status (:233); '409 REQUEST_MESSAGES.invalidTransition' for a second answer (:236); '409 REQUEST_MESSAGES.alreadyTerminal' for any transition from a terminal status (:243); '403 …notYoursToCancel' (:246); 'PATCH …/requests/{id} answers 403 …editForbidden' (:247); reassign 'answers 403 with the guard's fixed body' (:248). The only client-principal transition case, TC-02-INT-11 (:892), covers a message, answer, grant and decline and nothing else; no other case names a client user acting on a request. The Error Messages preamble (:576) says the table below lists 'Messages this spec's requirements and test cases assert without changing them' and then carries rows for exactly those six (:582, :586, :587, :590, :591, :592).

findings.suggestedFix: extend TC-02-INT-11, or add one case, covering: post to a terminal request (409 threadClosed), a second answer (409 invalidTransition), a transition from a terminal status (409 alreadyTerminal), cancel (403 notYoursToCancel), edit (403 editForbidden) and reassign (403, fixed body).

findings.claim: two of the three routes that must emit manageForbidden have no case, and the People list contract has no case at all

witness.detail: Requirement 9a (:120) names three routes that check manage-client-users in the service and 'refuse a staff caller who lacks it with 403 and CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.manageForbidden', and the Error Messages row (:570) names all three: 'GET …/clients/{clientId}/users, POST /api/invitations with role = client, PATCH …/users/{id}/remove'. TC-02-INT-02 (:816) asserts '403 manageForbidden' for the invitation route only. No case calls GET …/clients/{clientId}/users at any level, so the contract at :449-466 — the 200 body with `users` and `pendingInvitations`, the 403 and the 404 — has no observer, and no case asserts the remove route's 403 (TC-02-INT-06 removes as an admin who holds the capability).

findings.suggestedFix: add an integration case for GET …/clients/{clientId}/users covering its 200 body, its 403 manageForbidden for a staff caller without the capability and its 404 for a client of another organization, and assert the same 403 on the remove route.

findings.claim: the screen a client principal reaches on a staff URL is named but never stated, and nothing in the repository defines it

witness.detail: Edge case 8 (:528): 'The API answers 403; the screen shows the standard forbidden state and offers Requests.' This document defines no such state: the UI Description table (:602-611) has no row for it, the Required data-testid list (:613-628) carries no id for it, and no case asserts it. Nor is there one to inherit — `grep -rln forbidden apps/web/app apps/web/src` returns only apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/projects/[projectId]/board/BoardScreen.tsx, .../list/ListScreen.tsx, apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/time-tracking/TimeEntryModal.tsx and apps/web/src/members/ContractDetails.tsx, i.e. per-screen states, and apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/members/page.tsx has no 403 branch at all (its only error handling is the two remove/restore toasts at :92-117).

findings.suggestedFix: state what a client principal sees on a staff URL — the text, the control back to Requests and its data-testid — with a row in the UI Description table and a case, or delete the screen half of edge case 8 and let requirement 14's server answer be the whole rule.

findings.claim: the `user` half of the case cannot reach the screen it asserts on, so it passes whether or not the People section is gated

witness.detail: The steps (:1014) say 'Then open the same client's detail as a `user`' and the expected result (:1018) 'for the `user` neither the People section nor the invite control is drawn'. A `user` cannot open that screen: packages/validation/src/index.ts:706-707 gives the user role 'manage-clients': false and 'view-clients': false, and apps/api/src/clients/clients.service.ts getClient (:189) calls requireViewCapability, which is 'if (!can(caller.role, "view-clients")) { throw new NotFoundException(); }' (:371-372). The detail request answers 404, so both selectors are absent no matter how the People section is implemented.

findings.suggestedFix: drop the `user` half, or replace it with an observation that can fail — a direct call to GET …/clients/{clientId}/users as a `user` answering 403 manageForbidden, which is the rule the UI decision at :608 rests on.

findings.claim: the database the plan tells the next agent to use is on a port no tracked file publishes

witness.detail: The plan (:707): 'database `devscribed_e2e` at `localhost:5434`'. e2e/environment.ts:81 is `return 'postgresql://devscribed:devscribed@localhost:5433/devscribed_e2e';` and docker-compose.yml publishes one mapping, "- '5433:5432'". The only 5434 mapping is docker-compose.override.yml, which is ignored (`git check-ignore -v docker-compose.override.yml` -> '.gitignore:46') and untracked (`git ls-files docker-compose.override.yml` prints nothing), and its own header says 'Local-only port remap. Untracked'. A fresh checkout following this plan connects to nothing.

findings.suggestedFix: state `devscribed_e2e` at `localhost:5433`, which is what the tracked harness defaults to.

findings.claim: the sentence says the login refusal message is not restated here, and the document restates it three times

witness.detail: :597 'The login refusal message is spec 02 of user-management's and is **not** restated, changed, or duplicated here.' Requirement 6 (:98) quotes it: '400 {"message":"Your account has been deactivated. Contact your administrator."}', the login contract repeats it (:506) and the verification plan a third time (:717) — and AC-11 (:691) requires a case to assert that body byte for byte, which only works because the bytes are here.

findings.suggestedFix: delete the sentence; the body is stated where a case author needs it and that is the right outcome.

findings.symbol: Verification Plan, 'The refusal shape with no session at all'
findings.claim: a caller holding a session that cannot resolve a principal is not answered 401 by those routes

witness.detail: The row (:718) records 401 for an empty cookie jar and adds 'identical to a caller holding a session that cannot resolve a principal'. A caller with a valid cookie passes SessionGuard, which reads only Account.securityStamp (apps/api/src/auth/session.guard.ts:22-28); members and projects then refuse from their own lookup with 403, not 401 (apps/api/src/members/members.service.ts:274, apps/api/src/projects/projects.service.ts:688).

findings.suggestedFix: delete the trailing clause and keep the observed empty-jar result, which is what the row was walked for.

findings.claim: requirement 24 points at requirement 26 for the rule that lives in requirement 27

witness.detail: :211 'the client is simply no longer offered for new work (requirement 26)'. Requirement 26 (:219) is the project/client match and the projectRequiredForClient refusal; the rule that an archived client's users may not be chosen is requirement 27 (:224): 'Only an active client user of an active client may be chosen … a user of an archived client, is 400 with REQUEST_MESSAGES.clientUserUnavailable.' The Actors table gets it right at :43 ('requirement 27').

findings.suggestedFix: point at requirement 27, or drop the parenthetical.

findings.claim: the list of nav ids that must be absent for a client principal omits two the sidebar draws

witness.detail: :604 names 'nav-members, nav-projects, nav-clients, nav-time-tracking, nav-envelopes, nav-documents all absent'. `grep -n "testId: 'nav-" apps/web/src/layout/Sidebar.tsx` returns eight ids: nav-time-tracking (:64), nav-members (:75), nav-projects (:97), nav-clients (:108), nav-envelopes (:122), nav-documents (:131), nav-outbox (:140) and nav-settings (:159). nav-outbox is drawn wherever mail is simulated, which is every E2E run.

findings.suggestedFix: add nav-outbox and nav-settings to the absent list; requirement 12's 'exactly one row' already implies them, but a case author writes from this list.

findings.claim: the pending-invitation row is drawn but nothing addresses it

witness.detail: The client detail mock (:392) draws 'R. Ops … invited' and :609 requires the row 'Shown with status `invited`'. The People payload gives a pending invitation only '{ "email": …, "expiresAt": … }' (:464) — the same absence :609 itself records ('would need … an id on the pending payload') — and the Required data-testid list (:615-618) offers only client-user-row-{id} and client-user-row-{id}-status, keyed by an id a pending invitation does not have. No selector can assert the invited row.

findings.suggestedFix: give the pending row its own id — client-user-pending-row-{email} or equivalent — in the Required list, or say the invited row is not asserted.

findings.claim: what a client principal receives from the three client-user routes is not stated

witness.detail: Requirement 9a (:122) and the contracts (:455, :473, :482) state the refusal only for 'a staff caller' without the capability. A client principal passes SessionGuard and OrgScopeGuard on their own organization and these three routes carry no CapabilityGuard, so requirement 14's 'the API answers 403 for a capability-gated route' does not reach them; the permission matrix (:55) refuses the client user the capability but names no status or body.

findings.suggestedFix: say in requirement 9a that the service check refuses any caller who does not hold manage-client-users, whichever principal they are, with the same 403 and manageForbidden.

findings.claim: a clients-scoped route now answers a named 403 to a staff caller who lacks the capability, where the clients routes today answer 404 so the resource is not revealed

witness.detail: The contract (:455) refuses a staff caller without manage-client-users with '403 CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.manageForbidden'. apps/api/src/clients/clients.service.ts:365-373 collapses a missing client capability to NotFoundException instead, with the comment 'A missing capability collapses to 404 rather than 403 … so a distinctive 403 body would leak the fact that the resource exists.' A `user` calling the new route learns the client exists; calling the client detail they do not.

findings.suggestedFix: none required — recorded so a person can confirm the change of discipline on clients-scoped URLs was meant.
